title: Ainsworth Opens With a Statement
body:
Ainsworth put up the week's high score, 165.56, and it wasn't close - a 97.06-point beatdown of Zogg (68.5) that stands as the widest margin of the week. Glaser wasn't far behind with 152.9 in a win over Palaia, and Muenchow rolled past Pfaffinger 133.46-95.3.

Conlin needed only 129.86 to handle Hagan, who managed just 78.02 - the week's second-lowest score. The nightcap was the only real nail-biter: Larson held off Prodahl 101.86-87.92, a 13.94-point margin in an otherwise blowout-heavy opening week.

Goetz beat Stover 108.06-85.46 to round out the slate. Six games, five double-digit margins - Week 1 wasted no time separating the contenders from the rest.

title: Zogg Bounces Back, Three Teams Start 2-0
body:
A week after absorbing the league's worst beating, Zogg answered with the week's high score - 138.86 - to knock off Goetz (75.6) and get back in the win column. Ainsworth, Glaser, and Larson all won again to open the season 2-0, the only unbeaten teams left in the league.

Hagan bounced back from a rough Week 1 to beat Pfaffinger 105.06-70.9, and Larson handled Palaia 101.68-58.84 - the week's lowest score. The closest game of the week came at the bottom of the standings: Prodahl edged Stover 84.92-72.98, a 11.94-point margin.

Through two weeks, Pfaffinger, Palaia, and Stover are all 0-2 - and with Ainsworth (283.8 PF), Glaser (265.9 PF), and Larson (203.5 PF) all undefeated, the gap between the top and bottom of the league is already starting to show.
